meaning.evidence: All facts kept: the Sept. 4 lifting, July 15 closures, Aug. 28 partial restrictions, the 68°F (20°C) threshold, sunrise till 2 p.m., the angler guidance. "which can cook the fish and kill 'em" is colour on "lethal to fish".

sense.evidence: Mostly fits: "getting the flick" for lifted, "wet a line", "quick smart", "till the poor bugger's buggered" for to exhaustion, "let 'em get their breath back". "Fair go, fish in the coolest part of the day" strains: "fair go" pleads for fairness, not as a plain "please".

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like a real Australian ranger talking: "Staff'll keep an eye on the water temps", "Don't muck about playing a hooked trout", "Doing the right thing protects the park's fisheries".

register.evidence: A full, broad voice through every paragraph, as level 5 asks, with "bugger" well within uncle-bob.

tone.evidence: Keeps the notice's care for the fish, though the angler plea gets a cheeky edge: "till the poor bugger's buggered".

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Anglers can wet a line on these rivers, plus most of the park's other rivers, creeks and lakes, every day from sunrise to sunset".

variety.evidence: Varied: "the flick", "wet a line", "wound back", "cook the fish", "quick smart", "muck about", "get their breath back". "keep an eye on the water temps" repeats, as the original repeats.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the park notice and its update, structure kept.

problems.quote: Fair go, fish in the coolest part of the day
problems.original: Please fish during the coolest times of day
problems.why: "Fair go" is an appeal to fairness and reads oddly as "please".

A.summary: A full-voiced, natural, faithful retelling at the brief's weight; one strained "fair go".

meaning.evidence: All facts kept, with dates put in Australian order: "From Friday 4 September", "first shut to fishing altogether on 15 July", "from sunup till 2pm each day". "it might save them having to ban fishing" shifts the park's own voice to a third party, but the point survives.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "wound back to partial restrictions", "as conditions picked up", "quick smart", "till it's done in", "get their wind back", "Doing your bit".

authenticity.evidence: Natural Australian English throughout: "sunup to sundown", "so fishing's back on for part of the day", "all the creeks that feed them".

register.evidence: Clearly Aussie but measured, nearer level 3 than the level 5 asked: "Park staff will keep an eye on water temperatures." No swearing.

tone.evidence: Keeps the notice's practical concern whole: "Handle fish gently and keep them in the water as much as you can".

flow.evidence: Reads like it was written that way: "Cooler weather and water, plus rain in the current forecast, mean the full closures can come off."

variety.evidence: Varied: "wound back", "picked up", "go back in", "come off", "quick smart", "done in", "get their wind back".

essence.evidence: Clearly the original notice and update.

problems.quote: it might save them having to ban fishing
problems.original: may prevent the need to prohibit fishing
problems.why: The notice speaks for the park; "them" makes the ban someone else's.

problems.quote: Park staff will keep an eye on water temperatures.
problems.original: Staff will continue to monitor the water temperatures.
problems.why: A measured telling, lighter than level 5.

B.summary: A natural, faithful local retelling with the tone intact, lighter than the level-5 brief.

meaning.evidence: All facts kept, as the text is mostly the original: "Effective Friday, Sept. 4, the remaining fishing restrictions on the Firehole, Madison and Gibbon (downstream of Norris Campground) rivers and all associated tributaries will be lifted".

sense.evidence: The few changes are fillers and contractions with no sense to carry: "Mate,", "Mind ya,", "rivers'n all associated tributaries".

authenticity.evidence: Stock fillers bolted onto unaltered bureaucratic prose: "Mate, full fishing closures on these rivers were initially implemented July 15", "Anyway, Staff will continue to monitor", "Water temperatures 'ave cooled at night". "'ave" is Cockney.

register.evidence: Largely untranslated against a level-5 brief: "Temporary restrictions or closures may be implemented depending on condition assessments."

tone.evidence: The fillers make an official notice sound offhand: "Mind ya, Update: Yellowstone lifts full closures".

flow.evidence: Jarring joins: "Mind ya, Update:", "Now, Staff will continue", "as possible'n let them recover".

variety.evidence: Leans on sentence-opening fillers and "'n": "Now,", "Well,", "Anyway,", "Now, don't".

problems.original: Update: Yellowstone lifts full closures for Firehole, Madison and Gibbon rivers
problems.why: A filler stuck onto a headline breaks it.
